- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates or misses downward spikes; increase forecast buffer for downside risk.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-10 days; apply a “cool-down” correction to peak forecasts.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1-2% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.5, -0.3, +0.6), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.2 for 3+ days), model often underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to account for hidden support.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns bullish within 5 days, adjust forecast to reflect 10–15 day lag effect (i.e., forecast 10 days ahead should be 1–2% below true 30d outcome).
